# dsh-web-tools-deepseek
**English** · 简体中文
A provider bundle for the DeepSeek Harness (**DSH**) `ctx.web` seam. It routes `web_search` and `web
_fetch` to DeepSeek's own **native Search and Fetch APIs** instead of the model-backed web-search to
ol, and falls back to the native provider when the tools API fails or returns nothing.
The HTTP work lives in a small **Rust engine** (`crates/engine`, ~900 KiB) spoken to over NDJSON on
stdio; the cordis plugin is a thin JavaScript bridge around it.

## Why — and what it costs
DSH ships two web providers by default:
| | provider | how it works | billed |
| search | `deepseek-official` | a **server-side tool** (`web_search_20250305`) run inside the model

call | **tokens** — the results land in your context |
| fetch | `http` | fetches the URL locally,
anonymously | free |
This bundle replaces both with DeepSeek's dedicated endpoints:
| | endpoint | billed |

| search | `POST /v1/tools/search` | **¥5 per 1,000 successful requests** (≈ ¥0.005 each) |
| fetch
| `POST /v1/tools/fetch` | **¥5 per 1,000 successful requests** (≈ ¥0.005 each) |
> **Only successful requests are billed.** A request counts when it returns HTTP 200 *and* produced
a result — for search a non-empty `results`, for fetch page content. A 403, a 404, an empty result s
et, a timeout and a failed call are all **free**. `count` changes how many results you get, never th
e price. See Pricing and limits.
The trade: **a predictable per-call price instead of token cost**, plus search results that arrive a
s clean structured fields (`title` / `url` / `summary` / `date`) rather than as text the model has t
o parse out of its own tool output. To go back, see Rolling back.
### What the install does
The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so adding it appends to `dsh.profile.bundles` and its `cord
is.patch.yml` is applied. That patch:

1. **inserts** the plugin row (registering `deepseek-tools-api` for both search and fetch), and
2. *
*overrides the `web` row** so `searchProvider` and `fetchProvider` point at it.
Both halves are required. A patch entry **replaces that row's whole `config`** rather than deep-merg
ing it, so the override must restate *both* keys; and because three providers are then registered (`
deepseek-official`, `http`, `deepseek-tools-api`) the seam would otherwise refuse to guess and raise
`WEB_PROVIDER_AMBIGUOUS`.
**Restart DSH after installing.** Cordis re-runs `apply()` on a config reload, but the plugin *modul
e* is ESM-cached — code edits and a first mount need a process restart (verified experimentally; see
code edits and a first mount need a process restart (verified experimentally; see Troubleshooting).
### Requirements

| DSH | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop` 0.2.x (targets the `ctx.web` provider seam) |
| Node | ≥ 18.17 |

| Credential | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`, or a literal `apiKey` |
| Rust |
**not needed** — `bin/dsh-web-tools-deepseek-win32-x64.exe` is committed. Build it for Linux/macOS,
or take a release asset (zip uploads do not keep the executable bit: `chmod +x` it). |
### Why `snippetSource` defaults to `summary`
DeepSeek's documentation labels the two fields by consumer:
> `snippet` — short summary, relevant to the query, usually 100–200 characters, **suitable for front

-end display**.
> `summary` — long summary, relevant to the query, usually 600–800 characters, **sui
table for models to read**.
The only consumer of a DSH `WebSource` is a model, so `summary` is the faithful default even though
it costs several times the context (8 results ≈ 5K characters ≈ 2K tokens). Set `snippetSource: snip
mes the context (8 results ≈ 5K characters ≈ 2K tokens). Set `snippetSource: snippet` to spend less.
### Why `need_content` is never sent
`need_content: true` makes the API return each result's full page body in that result's `content` fi
eld — a payload the seam's closed `WebSource` type has nowhere to put, so it would be bytes paid for
and thrown away. (The API's own `curl` example includes `need_content: true`, which is easy to misr
ead as required; it is not.) Full page text comes from `web_fetch`, which is what it is for.

## Known limitations
* **Fetch 403 is common**, including for DeepSeek's own documentation site (measured: `api-docs.deep
seek.com` → `403 URL access denied`); `zh.wikipedia.org` and `news.ycombinator.com` measured `404 fa
iled to fetch URL`. DeepSeek states that fetch results depend on the target site's availability and
access policy — this is the service's verdict, not a plugin bug. Switch `fetchProvider` back to `htt

p` to fetch those sites.
* **No pagination** — one request returns at most 50 results and `truncated

` is always `false`.
* **No streaming or progress events** — a call resolves when the API answers.
*
**`need_content` is deliberately unused**, so page text always needs a second `fetch` call (and its

own ¥0.005).
* **The fallback target is read from a private seam field** (`ctx.web.searchProviders`
). There is no public way to look up another provider, and `ctx.web.search()` would recurse. If the
seam renames that field the fallback degrades to "no fallback", with a warning, rather than breaking

search.
* **The committed binary is Windows x64.** Other platforms build their own or take a releas
e asset; the workflow covers Windows, Linux and both macOS architectures. Release assets do not carr

y the executable bit, so `chmod +x` after downloading.
* **HTTP uses `reqwest` with `default-tls`**
(schannel on Windows), not rustls: a rustls crypto provider needs a C toolchain and NASM to build, w

hich would make `cargo build` fail on an ordinary machine.
* **`dsh --profile desktop --dump-config`
is unavailable** (`profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application`), so accep
tance evidence comes from live behaviour plus the wiring self-check log.
